effective_write_capability: shared workspace; sole mutation owner while dispatched
objective: Implement the smallest remaining adapter seam: one canonical RUN request protocol for script and argv that launches only through the validated split supervisor boundary, holds a prepared-child barrier until process-group and foreground verification, reports explicit exec-ready or exec-error acknowledgement, and maps these facts into ManagedLifecycle/host state without parent eval. Migrate focused lifecycle and launch runtime coverage to this common seam. Preserve existing public test APIs where practical and do not yet migrate unrelated input/jobs, hook, or takeover helpers unless required by the seam.
required_properties: Literal argv avoids shell reinterpretation; complex script is evaluated only by a child interpreter.
Parent shell remains in control wait and never evaluates payload.
PG_S and PG_E are same-session and distinct; foreground is read-back verified before the prepared child executes.
Exec success/failure has an explicit acknowledgement and failed exec does not launch a replacement shell.
Host lifecycle distinguishes accepted, supervisor ready, child prepared, experiment start, main return, descendant drain/unknown, input return, and control return.
STOPPED/CONTINUED and signal-derived statuses retain the validated semantics.
Bash-preferred and sh fallback launch selection remain fixed per session.
stop_conditions: The common protocol requires a new user-visible behavior decision.
Parent direct eval, shell support removal, or mandatory cgroup/extra privilege would be required.
No bounded implementation can establish explicit prepared/exec acknowledgement and host mapping without broad unrelated rewrites.
Owned process cleanup cannot be proven.
